sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 7 Status
sections.summary: Devnet 7 is stable with 100% participation; Teku has builder bid issues, and Besu and Geth bugs were fixed.
sections.body:
- Devnet 7 has been running stably with 100% participation, though a few payloads are missing and being investigated.
- Teku is mainly self-building blocks instead of using public bids, and bids are not coming in when Teku is used as a builder; Teku team asked to investigate.
  - Enrico (Teku) confirmed they are actively looking at the bid issues.
- Besu pushed a commit that broke stateless calculation, now fixed. All Besu regressions on devnet 7 are resolved.
- Geth had a builder-path bug that has also been fixed.
- PandaOps continues actively trying to break the network.
- A second round of spamming report was shared: [glamsterdam-devnet-7-self-built-blocks-round-2](https://panda-uploads-production.devops-539.workers.dev/panda/uploads/c761e4/glamsterdam-devnet-7-self-built-blocks-round-2.html)
- Very little community testing occurred on devnet 7 because the faucet was broken and no one raised the issue.

sections.heading: Repricing Benchmarks for Devnet 8
sections.summary: Repricing numbers are not yet final; clients asked to prioritize optimizations so results can be reassessed next week.
sections.body:
- Two parallel efforts underway: repricing analysis on devnet 7 with updated SIPs, and a full benchmark suite expected to produce results next week.
- The benchmarking team expanded pricing scenarios for SIL transfers and account access, and began using a new state-generation tool (state actor).
  - The previous Johamnet snapshot was found to be optimistically biased for some DB designs; the new state actor results are more accurate.
  - Some numbers got worse; unclear whether this is due to unmerged optimizations or expanded test scenarios.
- Maria stated she cannot confidently say the repricing numbers are final yet, and they could still require changes.
  - Key dashboard to monitor: [SIP-2780 repricing dashboard](https://misilva73.github.io/sip-2780-repricing/index.html)
- Since devnet 8 / Platåberget testnet is intended to be the last devnet and public-facing, Barnabas emphasized the need to finalize repricing before launch to avoid confusing number changes.
- Roll call of EL client optimization status:
  - Besu: all optimizations pushed to devnet 7; raised concern that state actor DB config doesn't match their sila-mainnet config — shared sila-mainnet config with benchmarking team.
  - Geth: no one from the relevant context available to answer; assumed no pending optimizations.
  - Nethermind: nothing currently planned, but would like to compare results across clients to identify further improvements.
  - ethrex: all optimizations ported to devnet 7.
  - Erigon: recently focused on correctness rather than optimization; benchmarking branch is outdated and being refreshed, with some regressions to resolve. Also adapting to the new benchmarking tooling.
  - Reth: nothing pending; everything merged.
- Agreement: clients should prioritize getting to at least 90% confidence on repricing numbers by next week so a decision on devnet 8 launch can be made at next ACDT.
- [Benchmarkoor run results](https://benchmarkoor.core.ethpandaops.io/suites/3f6a0898955dff4f) shared in chat.
- [Repricing SIPs updated in PR #12038](https://github.com/sila-chain/SIPs/pull/12038).

sections.heading: Discovery v5 Readiness
sections.summary: Discv5 appears ready for devnet 8; two clients still need the discv4-off flag, and ENR fields should be returned in admin_nodeInfo.
sections.body:
- Previous agreement was to enable discv5 in releases while keeping discv4 on, then test turning discv4 off — this is what devnet 8 will test.
- Csaba tested with other clients in a Kurtosis testnet; an apparent Nethermind sync issue turned out to be a cherry-pick problem on the devnet 7 branch, not a real issue.
- Two clients are still missing the flag to turn off discv4, but adding it should be straightforward.
- Some clients need to reconstruct branches or cherry-pick to include discv5-only support.
- CL implementations have been running discv5 for a long time, so EL implementations sharing the same library are not expected to have major issues.
- A bootstrap issue was encountered in Kurtosis where bootnode addresses were still being passed as enode URLs instead of ENR — both Csaba and Barnabas have fixes for this.
- Barnabas requested that EL clients return ENR fields (in addition to or instead of enode fields) in the `admin_nodeInfo` RPC endpoint; currently all clients return only enode.
- Reth confirmed discv5 changes are partially merged with remaining work in PR form, expected to be ready soon.
- Broader discussion of sunsetting discv4 on sila-mainnet flagged for a future call before sila-mainnet launch.
- Hive tests exist for discv5 that all clients should work toward passing.

sections.heading: Platåberget Testnet Proposal
sections.summary: Devnet 8 will be launched as a public named testnet called Platåberget, running for a couple of months until the Glamsterdam sila-mainnet fork.
sections.body:
- PandaOps proposed converting devnet 8 into a short-lived public testnet named "Platåberget" (internally still devnet-8 as a CNAME).
  - Motivation: naming a testnet rather than using a devnet number encourages broader community attention and testing.
- The testnet would run approximately until the Glamsterdam sila-mainnet fork, then be sunset.
- Prerequisite: all repricing numbers must be finalized before launch.
- After launch, approximately a week to 10 days before the fork to give builders time to prepare.
- Separate NFT devnets will continue for large-scale internal testing and chaos engineering.
- No objections raised to proceeding with the testnet approach.
- Exact launch timing TBD; decision expected at next ACDT call.
- A blog post announcing the testnet is planned.
- MEV relays and builders are being contacted to participate on the testnet; a mix of builders and relays is desired.
- Community testing and app developers are encouraged to use Platåberget as their testing ground.
- For devnet-8, trunk branches can be used instead of custom branches.

sections.heading: PFI: SIP-8115, SIP-8116, SIP-7807 (Etan)
sections.summary: Three SIPs proposed: batch priority fees at block end, replace cumulative receipt gas with per-tx gas, and SSZ-based block hash.
sections.body:
- [SIP-8115](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-8115): Batch priority fees at end of block.
  - Currently priority fees are credited to the fee recipient after every transaction; proposal collects them and credits once at block end.
  - Benefits: slightly better parallel transaction execution (no write conflict on fee recipient per tx), cleaner UX for block producers (one entry instead of hundreds of micro-credits).
  - Downside: priority fee only spendable in the next block.
- [SIP-8116](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-8116): Replace cumulative receipt fields with per-transaction gas used.
  - Current receipts store cumulative gas used up to and including the transaction; to get individual tx gas used, you must download two receipts and compute the difference.
  - Proposal replaces cumulative field with individual tx gas used, making trust-minimized verification via Merkle proofs simpler.
  - Jochem noted this must account for the dual gas dimensions (state gas and execution gas) introduced by SIP-8037; Etan agreed the SIP can be updated to include both.
  - Simon (Besu) noted individual tx gasUsed is already in the execution-APIs spec and served by clients, but Etan clarified it is not committed on-chain, so it cannot be verified with a Merkle proof.
- [SIP-7807](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-7807): SSZ execution blocks (scoped down to block hash only).
  - Originally proposed as a headliner and rejected; now reduced to only changing how the block hash is computed to use SSZ.
  - Benefits: users can prove individual header fields without downloading full header; CL can compute block hash locally instead of sending every block to EL for verification, improving CL sync.
  - Also removes logs bloom from block header hash (JSON-RPC returns all-ones for backward compatibility).
  - Dependency list significantly reduced from original proposal.
  - Toni asked about interaction with SIP-7778 regarding gas_used in receipts; Etan confirmed it should be the user-facing gas after refunds.

sections.heading: PFI: SIP-7819 SETDELEGATE Instruction
sections.summary: SIP-7819 proposes a SETDELEGATE opcode to create cheap 7702-style delegate proxies from contracts, reducing smart account deployment costs.
sections.body:
- [SIP-7819](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-7819): Proposed by Hadrien (OpenZeppelin), presented by Derek.
- Motivation: Glamsterdam makes state creation ~5x more expensive, significantly impacting account abstraction since every new smart account creates new state via minimal proxy deployment.
- SIP-7702 introduced a native 23-byte delegate pointer (3-byte prefix + 20-byte address), but it can only be set via a special transaction type, making it non-composable on-chain.
- SIP-7819 introduces a new opcode `SETDELEGATE` that allows contracts (e.g., factories) to create accounts with 7702-style delegate pointers, enabling on-chain composability.
  - Acts as a factory opcode like CREATE and CREATE2.
  - Result: much cheaper proxy account creation, beneficial for account abstraction adoption.
- Difference from DELEGATECALL: currently proxies must deploy bytecode (hundreds of bytes) and do an SLOAD for upgradeability; SETDELEGATE sets only 23 bytes of code and gets upgradeability for free if the factory supports it.
- Jochem expressed enthusiasm for the SIP, noting current delegate proxy deployment will be more expensive in Glamsterdam.
- Gary raised mempool validation concerns: with SETDELEGATE, contracts can perform authorizations via opcode making it harder to detect without execution, unlike SIP-7702's explicit auth list.
- Barnabas asked whether 7819 makes sense if frames are adopted; Derek confirmed it is purely orthogonal to frames.
- lightclient suggested the designator should differentiate 7702 accounts vs contracts.

sections.heading: PFI: SIP-7906 Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcodes
sections.summary: SIP-7906 proposes opcodes (TXTRACE, TXDIFF, EVENTDATACOPY) to expose state diffs in a post-transaction frame, enabling enforceable transaction outcome assertions.
sections.body:
- [SIP-7906](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-7906): Proposed by Alex Forshtat for Hegotá inclusion.
- Problem: transaction outcomes are unpredictable for users; inputs plus current state determine outcomes, and users have no on-chain control over what actually happens. This enables account takeovers, drainers, fake DEXs, aggressive MEV, and front-running.
  - Referenced the Bybit $1.5 billion loss as a prominent example.
- Existing mitigations are insufficient:
  - Off-chain simulations are best-effort, can be stale, are proprietary, and can themselves be attack vectors.
  - On-chain guard modules are limited without native EVM support — cannot express negative conditions ("nothing changed except X") and cannot observe proxy implementation addresses or iterate over all assets.
- SIP-7906 introduces three opcodes:
  - `TXTRACE`: iterator over all state changes (follows shape of debug_traceTransaction); absence of an entry means that change did not happen, enabling negative constraints.
  - `TXDIFF`: direct access to specific storage slots and variables of any contract; also acts as SLOAD alias for unchanged slots.
  - `EVENTDATACOPY`: exposes event data for protocols relying on events (relays, bundlers, bridges).
- Uses SIP-8141 frames: opcodes only work in a new "post-transaction" frame mode that runs after transaction finalization; the only decision possible is to revert or accept the entire transaction.
- Implementation complexity is low given SIP-8141: state diffs are already collected by all nodes, just need to be exposed to the frame.
- Already implemented by ethrex with a [public devnet](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex/blob/hegota-devnet/scripts/hegota-devnet/USER-GUIDE.md) and a [playground demo](https://eip7906.forshtat.com/).
  - [ethrex PR #6891](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex/pull/6891)
- lightclient strongly endorsed the value of transaction assertions, citing overwhelming demand from users of all sizes.
- Marius (Geth) expressed preference for exposing journal access with a different/simpler API, specifically favoring TXDIFF alone without TXTRACE.
  - lightclient agreed the TXTRACE suite may not be necessary; just TXDIFF is fairly straightforward.
  - Marius noted SIP-7906 has changed significantly since last discussed in a breakout and is "against making the EVM simple and easy to reason about."
  - Alex defended TXTRACE as necessary for open-ended negative constraints; acknowledged TXDIFF could adopt some TXTRACE fields.
- Csaba expressed support for TXDIFF as it handles atomicity well.
- Discussion to continue on Sila Magicians and via the clear signing work group.

sections.heading: PFI: SIP-7668 Remove Bloom Filters
sections.summary: SIP-7668 proposes removing log bloom filters from headers and receipts, saving computation on data that is no longer used.
sections.body:
- [SIP-7668](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-7668): Proposed by Jochem for Hegotá.
- Log bloom filters are no longer useful, yet all clients still compute them during re-execution — a waste of resources.
- Overlaps with SIP-7807 (SSZ block hash) which also removes the bloom from the block header, but SIP-7668 also covers the bloom in receipts.
  - If both SIPs advance, they could be combined or one could defer to the other.
- Works well alongside [SIP-8304](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-8304) (log and transaction index), which does not itself remove bloom filters.
- Etan clarified that his SIP-7807 only removes the header bloom (replacing with all-ones in JSON-RPC), while SIP-7668 also targets the receipt bloom.

sections.heading: PFI: SIP-8200 EVMification of Precompiles
sections.summary: SIP-8200 proposes replacing rarely-used precompiles with EVM bytecode equivalents, simplifying ZKVM circuits and reducing attack surface.
sections.body:
- [SIP-8200](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-8200): Proposed by Kevaundray Wedderburn.
- Analysis of 99% of blocks shows ~50% of precompiles are barely used; Blake2F is essentially used by one contract.
  - [Precompile usage data](https://sil-act.github.io/evmification-data/index.html)
- For ZKVMs, each precompile requires a dedicated accelerator/circuit, increasing audit surface and complexity. EVMification removes this burden.
- Secondary benefit: clients can remove native precompile libraries once EVMified.
- Implementation: set EVM bytecode at the precompile address as equivalent code.
- This is an implicit repricing — the EVM bytecode cost may differ from current precompile gas schedules.
  - The data site shows impact of 2x and 5x cost increases; some contracts break badly at higher costs.
  - Only precompiles that are basically unused are included to avoid user impact; BLS12-381 precompiles were removed from scope because optimized bytecode was unavailable and usage, while low, exists.
- Toni asked why not just reprice precompiles to EVM-equivalent cost and let clients keep native implementations. Kev explained that precompile costs are often dynamic/input-dependent, making it difficult to reprice without the actual bytecode in consensus.
- Jochem suggested that if BLS precompiles are to be deprecated, an SIP should signal this; acknowledged this would be contentious since BLS precompiles were added only one or two forks ago.
- Jochem noted [SIP-7666](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-7666) (EVMify IDENTITY precompile) should also be PFI'd for Hegotá alongside SIP-8200.
- Marius quipped that the 19 BLS precompiles not being used was unsurprising.

sections.heading: SIP Process Housekeeping
sections.summary: Glamsterdam SIPs are being moved to SFI and Review status; authors asked to approve pending PRs so Meta SIP-7773 can advance.
sections.body:
- From the last meeting, all Glamsterdam upgrade SIPs can be moved to SFI (Scheduled for Inclusion); a PR is open but pending author approvals.
- Some core SIPs also need to be promoted to Review status; most authors have approved except SIP-8038.
- 5 new PRs were opened to move non-core SIPs (networking, informational) listed in the meta SIP to Review status; 4 are still awaiting approval.
- Once all listed SIPs reach Review status, SIP-7773 (Glamsterdam meta SIP) can be moved to Review at the next ACD meeting.
- Authors urged to review and approve the pending PRs.
- Reference: [Pooja's process housekeeping comment](https://github.com/sila-chain/pm/issues/2166#issuecomment-5108689733).
